claims.text: The as-deposited Nb25Mo25Ta25W25 film is a single-BCC-phase, columnar nanocrystalline material.
The as-deposited Nb20Mo20Ta20W20Re20 film is a single-BCC-phase, columnar nanocrystalline material.
The Nb25Mo25Ta25W25 and Nb20Mo20Ta20W20Re20 films have thicknesses of 3.3 and 2.3 micrometers, respectively.
Adding Re to NbMoTaW refines its grain structure.
Adding Re to NbMoTaW increases lattice distortion.
Adding Re to NbMoTaW increases excess free volume.
The Re-containing alloy has several-nanometer-wide amorphous regions at grain boundaries.
Re-induced microstructural modifications provide additional defect-sink sites.
The additional defect sinks accelerate annihilation of irradiation-induced vacancies.
Accelerated vacancy annihilation suppresses helium-bubble accumulation, growth, and segregation.
Helium-bubble accumulation, growth, and segregation promote grain-boundary embrittlement and irradiation hardening.
After the specified helium irradiation, NbMoTaWRe is predicted to have smaller and more uniformly distributed helium bubbles than NbMoTaW.
After the specified helium irradiation, NbMoTaWRe is predicted to exhibit less irradiation-induced hardening than NbMoTaW.
After the specified helium irradiation, NbMoTaWRe is predicted to exhibit less severe grain-boundary embrittlement than NbMoTaW.
The proposed comparison uses 120 keV He2+ implantation at a fluence of 1 × 10^16 ions/cm^2 and a dose rate of 1 × 10^13 ions/cm^2/s for 1000 seconds.
Under the specified implantation conditions, the damage zone is confined to approximately 400 nm.
The anticipated benefit is limited to magnetron-sputtered NbMoTaW-based films irradiated at room temperature under the specified implantation conditions.
Generalization beyond the specified compositions, microstructures, and irradiation conditions is not established.
The proposed falsification experiment compares identically processed Re-free and Re-containing films using TEM, nanoindentation, and in-situ micropillar compression.
Failure of NbMoTaWRe to show improved bubble characteristics, reduced hardening, and reduced grain-boundary embrittlement relative to NbMoTaW would reject the hypothesis.
